question: If cos 53° = x over y , then sec 53° + cot 37° is equal to:
solution:
**Concept:**

In a right-angled triangle ABC

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e8a276c5607a5e51b77f19a997e9430c5ce95d62d9f8f978dd239e09376fa32.png] 

cos θ = bover h

sec θ = 1over cosθ = hover b

tan θ = sin θ over cosθ = pover b

**Calculation:**

cos 53° = xover y

sec 53° = yover x

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a9231b7b413cb39f66cda50003731140e36612b71e4c88799d5d7042d624e16.png] 

cot 37° = 1over tan 37° = {sqrt {(y²-x²)}}over{x}

Using the value of sec 53° and cot 37°-

⇒ sec 53° + cot 37° = yover x + {sqrt (y²-x²)}over x = frac{{y + sqrt {{y²} - {x²}} }}{x}

∴ **The value of the expression is frac{{y + sqrt {{y²} - {x²}} }}{x}**.
